facts.statement: Dinosuchus is an extinct genus of alligatorid crocodilian.
facts.quote: Dinosuchus is a genus of extinct alligatorid crocodilian.

facts.statement: The genus was first described in 1876 based on a vertebra found in the Brazilian Amazon, with the type species named D. terror.
facts.quote: The genus was first described in 1876 on the basis of a vertebra from the Brazilian Amazon, the type species being named D. terror.

facts.statement: A new species, D. neivensis, was named in 1921 based on a large mandible discovered in Colombia.
facts.quote: In 1921, a new species of Dinosuchus, D. neivensis, was named based on a large mandible that was discovered in Colombia.

facts.statement: D. neivensis was later found to be synonymous with Brachygnathosuchus braziliensis and Purussaurus brasiliensis and was reassigned in 1924 to P. brasiliensis.
facts.quote: D. neivensis was later found to be synonymous with both Brachygnathosuchus braziliensis and Purussaurus brasiliensis, being reassigned in 1924 to the senior synonym P. brasiliensis.

facts.statement: The name Dinosuchus was used in 1936 by Robert Broom for a dinocephalian therapsid from South Africa.
facts.quote: In 1936, Robert Broom used the name Dinosuchus for a dinocephalian therapsid from South Africa.

facts.statement: Dinosuchus should not be confused with Deinosuchus, a large non-crocodilian Eusuchian from Late Cretaceous North America.
facts.quote: It is not to be confused with Deinosuchus, a large non-crocodilian Eusuchian from Late Cretaceous North America.

facts.statement: The parent group of Dinosuchus is Alligatoridae.
Dinosuchus belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
Dinosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
Dinosuchus lived from the Tortonian to the Messinian, between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Messinian (11.63 to 5.333 million years ago)

facts.statement: The fossil range of Dinosuchus is the Late Miocene to Late Pliocene (Montehermosan-Uquian).

rejected.statement: Dinosuchus was very large among alligatorids, except for the giant caiman Purussaurus and its closest relatives.
rejected.quote: It was very large compared to other alligatorids, save for the giant caiman Purussaurus and its closest relatives.

rejected.statement: Broom's Dinosuchus is now considered a junior synonym of Anteosaurus.
